answer: Time-locked reputation decay. Each identity accrues trust slowly along a vine of verified interactions; cloning resets that growth to zero, so a fresh clone must re-earn standing from scratch. Honest agents retain accumulated history while attacker's copies each bear the full ramp-up delay, and any shared payoff splitting makes the clone's per-identity return sit below the honest path. A knoll of old reputation also lets peers weight matches by age, so new copies start invisible. Every hop through a mirror check doubles the attacker's onboarding latency.
